messages:
Anna (CS): heads up — AquilaHealth saw 3 repeat 503s this week, highest volume Wed 09:32 UTC. page came in, but reopening here to track customer-facing actions.
Matthew (CSM): thanks. customer reports degraded throughput and higher latency during their heavy syncs. they flagged a billing spike too. cc @Kevin
Kevin (Oncall): looking at the infra alerts now, I see a burst of queued requests -> backend timeouts. pulling logs.
SaaS Metrics Bot: Alert: AquilaHealth - 503 spike: 2026-02-11 09:32 -> 09:42 UTC, 42 errors in 10m, p95 latency 1.3s :warning:
Kevin (Oncall): quick log sample:
```
{"req_id":"f4a9b2","ts":"2026-02-11T09:33:04Z","model":"xlarge-prod","status":503,"err":"kv-cache-miss+timeout","lat_ms":1298}
{"req_id":"f4a9b3","ts":"2026-02-11T09:33:06Z","model":"xlarge-prod","status":503,"err":"kv-cache-miss+timeout","lat_ms":1342}
```
Kevin (Oncall): looks like repeated KV-cache misses combined with short-lived GPU overheating leading to retries. ops mitigated with a rolling restart at 09:38 which dropped errors. tagging @Rachel for model/runtime angle.
Rachel (Eng): yep i saw the restart. root cause likely twofold: (1) cache eviction threshold too aggressive for their sequence distribution, (2) quick GPU thermal throttling on a single host. i'll propose changes.
Anna (CS): customer wants a written summary + ETA for fix. also they asked about whether this could recur during their month-end sync next week.
Rachel (Eng): proposed plan:
- short term (today): increase KV cache size for Aquila routing pool + relax eviction to 10% higher. owner: Rachel. ETA: 24h.
- short term infra: pin Aquila traffic away from the host with recent thermal throttles. owner: Kevin. ETA: 3h.
- medium term (next sprint): implement cache warmup for large prefix workloads and add an alert on host thermal events integrated into the incident pipeline. owner: Eng Infra. ETA: 2 weeks.
Matthew (CSM): can we also add a customer-facing mitigation note I can send? something like: "we increased cache allocation and routed your traffic to a stable host; we will monitor through your month-end sync and follow up" — is that accurate? :eyes:
Rachel (Eng): yes that's accurate. also will add a watch rule to alert us if p95 > 1s for >5m.
Anna (CS): action items summary for tracking:
- Rachel: apply cache size change + confirm baseline metrics after change. due: +24h. (owner assigned)
- Kevin: re-route away from thermally-troubled host and confirm stability. done by +3h.
- Matthew: send mitigation note to customer once Rachel confirms change applied. due: after Rachel confirmation.
- Anna: open renewal-risk flag in CRM and set check-in for day after month-end sync. due: today EOD.
Deploy Bot: deploy started: change-set #6532 roll-forward cache config for aquila-pool -> status: in-progress
Kevin (Oncall): re-route complete, host removed from pool at 09:41 UTC. monitoring looks stable so far. :thumbsup:
Rachel (Eng): cache tweak applied at 10:05 UTC, watching metrics. will post a short perf snapshot in this thread once we have 30m of data.
SaaS Metrics Bot: AquilaHealth p95 latency: before change 1.32s -> 30m after change 0.48s, 503 rate dropped to 1 in 30m. :white_check_mark:
Matthew (CSM): I'll send the mitigation note now and schedule a proactive check during their month-end. Thanks team. 
Anna (CS): great. tagging owners in our tracker and will close this thread once post-month-end check passes. :rocket:
